transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

The 4C code on your Samsung dishwasher indicates a water supply issue, meaning it isn't getting enough fresh water to start the cycle. This is often caused by simple things like the tap being turned off or the hose being blocked. Please check that the water tap connected to the dishwasher is fully open and that the inlet hose at the back isn't kinked or trapped behind the machine.
Ok. The valve under the sink for the dishwasher is a slot-head one and the slot is at 90 degrees, so I think it's turned off. The hose has no kinks. Should I turn it on?

A slot at 90 degrees to the pipe means the valve is closed. Yes, please turn it fully on so the slot aligns with the pipe. Once that's done, try starting a cycle again and let me know if the 4C code clears or if it still appears.
Ok, I've turned the valve on so the slot lines up with the pipe and started a cycle. It's filling with water now and running normally, no 4C.

That is excellent news. The 4C code was simply because the isolation valve was closed, preventing water from entering the machine. To avoid this happening again, just remember that a slot at 90 degrees to the pipe means 'off', so always ensure it aligns with the pipe for 'on'. If you have any other questions or need help with anything else, just let me know.
